channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Breaking: UoM Consumer Sentiment Index comes at 46.3 in October
item.description: American consumer confidence declined in early October, as households grew more pessimistic about current conditions and the broader economic outlook, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan.

item.title: Gold: Short covering signals renewed bullish momentum - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek highlight that CTAs (Commodity Trading Advisors) are covering Gold shorts, with positioning rising by around 7% of maximum historical size. They note renewed inflows into Chinese Gold ETFs after the holiday and continued global ETF demand.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen keeping hike option open – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research anticipates India’s September inflation to rise to 5.7% year-on-year from 4.8%, driven by broad-based food price gains and higher non-food fuel costs. Core inflation is expected to tick up as uneven monsoon conditions and elevated Oil prices add pressure, leading DBS to expect the RBI to keep the door open for a possible rate hike in December 2026.

item.title: European Central Bank: Conditional support and French risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Economist Maartje Wijffelaars describes widening French spreads and notes 38% of French high-grade corporate debt now yields less than government bonds. She argues most spread widening may be over as France is seen as too big to fail and ECB tools exist. She outlines ECB conditionality for TPI and stresses France’s need for a credible budget.

item.title: Canadian Dollar underperforms after Canada sheds 68.3K jobs in September
item.description: USD/CAD climbs on Friday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) weakens sharply following a disappointing domestic employment report. A firm US Dollar (USD) provides additional support to the pair. At the time of writing, USD/CAD trades around 1.4276, at levels last seen in April 2025.

item.title: United States: Core CPI trend seen moderating – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ US economics team led by Oscar Munoz, with Eli Nir, Gennadiy Goldberg and Molly Brooks, expects September Core CPI to slow to 0.20% month-on-month, driven by softer core services and supercore.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Rate hike risks support currency – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman notes that the Norwegian Krone (NOK) is softer against most peers following a modest pullback in Oil prices, but September CPI data keep further Norges Bank rate hikes in play, offering support to NOK. Sticky underlying inflation above the central bank’s forecasts means the option to raise rates further remains open, with markets pricing roughly 50% odds of another hike by year-end.

item.title: Breaking: Canada Unemployment Rate rises to 6.5% in September as expected
item.description: The Unemployment Rate in Canada edged higher to 6.5% in September from 6.4% in August, Statistics Canada reported on Friday. This reading came in line with analysts' estimate.

item.title: Gold recovery stalls near $4,200 as US Dollar, Treasury yields stabilise
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the front foot on Friday but struggles to extend its advance as the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields show signs of stabilisation following Thursday’s sharp pullback.

item.title: British Pound gains ground as Japanese Yen underperforms
item.description: GBP/JPY trades with a mild positive bias on Friday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) underperforms across the board. A pause in the global bond sell-off has pushed government bond yields lower, with Japanese yields falling more sharply than their UK counterparts.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Choppy trade inside defined range – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/JPY has been volatile around 157.86, with swings between 157.51 and 158.36 failing to establish a clear trend. For the coming sessions, the pair is expected to trade within 157.50–158.50 intraday, while the 1–3 week view favours consolidation in a narrower 157.00–158.70 band against a backdrop of longer-term downside momentum.

item.title: Oil: Iran tensions keep crude prices elevated - Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Economist Maartje Wijffelaars notes Oil prices climbed to around $105 per barrel as Iran struck tankers, before Brent eased after US comments on talks with Iran. Despite the pullback, Oil and diesel remain elevated, with Gasoil sharply higher since Tuesday.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Rallies fail above 1.1200 amid high Oil prices, debt woes
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is failing to capitalise on the moderate US Dollar (USD) weakness witnessed on Friday as the high Oil prices and the ongoing concerns about France’s public debt offset investors’ optimism about lower global yields.

item.title: Indian Rupee attracts bids as US bond yields cool down
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades slightly higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR pair corrects to near 96.55, but is still close to its all-time high of 97.00. The Indian currency gets a much-needed reprieve from a corrective move in United States (US) Treasury Yields.

item.title: Japanese Yen underperforms against its peers into the weekend
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) trades lower against its major currency peers on Friday. In the European trade, the USD/JPY pair is up 0.3% to near 158.25.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Labor data may trigger dovish repricing – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman highlights that USD/CAD is consolidating just above 1.4200 after touching fresh cyclical highs near 1.4300. Canada’s September labor force survey is the key release, with modest job gains and a higher unemployment rate expected.

item.title: Euro: Elusive recovery prospects against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING observes that EUR/USD has moved back above 1.120 on Dollar softness, but the Euro still struggles against other European currencies as markets keep pricing a French fiscal premium. He argues that French political and bond-market risks may persist, and ING still sees scope for EUR/USD to test the 1.110/1.112 area in the near term.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Banxico cautious on cuts as Peso risks linger – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke notes Banxico’s September minutes signal a board leaning toward further easing, though the policy rate stayed at 6.5%. He argues it is too early to see a clear November cut, given US elections, geopolitical risks and energy prices.

item.title: US Dollar: Upside risks persist with strong demand – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that a modest pullback in energy prices has eased the global bond sell-off and slowed the recent Dollar rally. However, he stresses that US growth outperformance and strong foreign appetite for US securities keep USD risks skewed to the upside.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Policy divergence weighs on CAD against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence note that the recent USD/CAD rally reflects broad US Dollar (USD) strength rather than specific Canadian Dollar (CAD) weakness, with the pair consolidating near 1.425 after failing to break 1.43.

item.title: Australian Dollar struggles to extend gains to near 0.7000, US CPI comes into focus
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is up 0.3% at around 0.6980 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday. However, the pair is struggling to extend gains beyond 0.6990.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD rallies to $4,200 as US yields retreat
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) accelerates its recovery on Friday, favoured by a softer US Dollar, amid a moderate pullback in US yields.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Range trade bias holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CHF shows slightly increased downside momentum, with scope to test 0.8290 but limited odds of a sustained break lower. For the coming days, they maintain that USD/CHF has likely entered a range-trading phase between 0.8245 and 0.8365, while over the 1–3 month horizon they see the pair continuing to rebound but lacking strength to revisit the July peak.

item.title: Euro: China trade tensions and CNY strength pose downside risks - MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Derek Halpenny highlights Europe's economic resilience following Germany's upward Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth revisions but warns that potential European Union (EU) import restrictions and additional tariffs on Chinese goods could escalate trade tensions and weigh on the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Romanian Leu: Coalition hopes support RON assets – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note the National Bank of Romania (NBR) kept its policy rate at 6.50% and reinforced a hawkish stance as earlier inflation risks are now part of the baseline.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $60.40 per troy ounce, up 2.06% from the $59.19 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish NBP signals weigh on PLN – Commerzbank
item.description: Tatha Ghose at Commerzbank describes NBP Governor Glapinski’s latest press conference as a net dovish surprise versus expectations for a clearer hike signal.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs data and BoC path – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects Canada’s September jobs report to show a modest payroll rebound and slightly higher unemployment, not enough to justify an October Bank of Canada hike. He notes that a December move is fully priced, while USD/CAD remains dominated by the Dollar, with a sustained move below 1.420 seen as requiring better global bond conditions.

item.title: Euro extends recovery due to relief from drop in French bond yields
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends Thursday’s recovery move against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. In the European trade, the EUR/USD pair is up 0.2% higher to near 1.1235. The Euro rebounds as yields offered on France bonds have corrected sharply.

item.title: British Pound: Mild downside bias against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann observe that GBP/USD has held modest gains around 1.3230, but recent guidance from the Bank of England on higher-for-longer rates has not translated into a clear bullish trend.
